title: Marechkawick
summary: Marechkawick names a Native village associated with the site of Brooklyn in early Dutch colonial records. Recorded spellings include Marychkenwikingh, Merechkawick, Merchkawikingh, and Rechkewick. Reckkewick is a cross-reference form associated with the same Brooklyn landscape.
map_geometry_source: Approximate modern Downtown Brooklyn/Gowanus-area point based on Tooker entry; not an exact historical coordinate.
history_content: Marechkawick is connected with leaders Seyseys and Numers, land near the Hell Gate islands, and later references near the Kill of Gouwanes. The name appears in a documentary landscape shaped by Dutch expansion, diplomacy, conflict, and Native community continuity in western Long Island.
translation_content:
The name is interpreted as meaning "at his fortified or palisadoed house," connecting it with a sachem residence or headquarters. Recorded forms include Marychkenwikingh, Merchkawikingh, Merechkawick, Reckkenweck, Reckkenwick, Rechkewick, Maerckaawicks, Marechkawieck, and Marwechkawick.

Why Place Names Matter

“Through place naming, communities have the opportunity to unlock past stories, preserve traditions, and provide a sense of belonging and identity.”

— NSW Aboriginal Languages Trust, NSW Aboriginal Languages Week 2025 Education Presentation Notes (2025), Slide 6: Place-names in Aboriginal Languages
whereintheworld_content: This blue marker is an approximate general-location point for Downtown Brooklyn near the historic Gowanus area. It is not an exact historic village coordinate.
